rows.title: use Contextmanagers to handle StopIteration in generators

outcomes.text: The @contextmanager decorator is used here but `contextmanager` is not imported in this module. Add `from contextlib import contextmanager` to the imports.

When converting a generator used with `yield from` into a context manager, the function must `yield` exactly once and handle cleanup in a `try/finally`. Verify that the body of `_runtest_for` follows the contextmanager protocol; otherwise the `with self._runtest_for(...):` blocks may misbehave.
Changelog filenames should use the issue number they fix, not the PR number. If this change addresses issue #XYZ, rename the file accordingly (e.g., `XYZ.bugfix.rst`).

rows.title: terminal: notify terminal emulator about test session progress

outcomes.text: The AUTHORS list is expected to be kept in alphabetical order. Adding "Anna Tasiopoulou" after "Anita Hammer" breaks that ordering; please insert the name in the correct position.

Registering the `TerminalProgressPlugin` inside `mywriter` means the plugin could be registered multiple times if `mywriter` is called more than once during configuration. Consider moving the registration to a dedicated hook (e.g., `pytest_configure`).
`write_raw` duplicates the Unicode‑encode error handling logic from `write`. It would be simpler and less error‑prone to have `write` call `write_raw` after markup, avoiding code duplication.
The test module uses `StringIO` but does not import it. Add `from io import StringIO` to the imports.

`Mock(spec=pytest.TerminalReporter)` is incorrect because `TerminalReporter` lives in `_pytest.terminal`, not in the public `pytest` namespace. Use `Mock(spec=_pytest.terminal.TerminalReporter)` (import the class) to get a proper spec.

The parametrization list for `test_plugin_registration` is syntactically broken – there is an incomplete tuple starting with `("`. This will cause a syntax error. Fix the tuple or remove the stray line.

rows.title: don't crash if exceptiongroup has only hidden tb frames

outcomes.text: The local variable name `traceback` shadows the standard library module `traceback`. Consider renaming it (e.g., `tb`) to avoid confusion and potential import issues.
`reprtraceback.extraline` is set unconditionally when `traceback` is empty, but `reprtraceback` may be `None` in some code paths. Ensure the object always has this attribute or guard the assignment.

The f‑string used to generate the test file includes leading indentation from the source file, which can affect the generated code. Using `textwrap.dedent` or a raw string without indentation would make the test more robust.

The assertion checks for `*ValueError: bar` even when `group=True`, where the raised exception is an `ExceptionGroup`. This may be flaky on different Python versions; consider matching either `ValueError` or `ExceptionGroup` in the output.

rows.title: Ensure subtest's context kwargs are JSON serializable

outcomes.text: Missing import: `saferepr` is used in `__post_init__` but not imported. Add `from _pytest._io.saferepr import saferepr` at the top of the module.

`_to_json` now creates a temporary `result` variable only to return it unchanged. This adds unnecessary indirection; you can simply `return dataclasses.asdict(self)` unless you plan to extend the method later.

rows.title: docs: clarify capture fixture precedence over -s

outcomes.text: The new ``.. _accessing-captured-output:`` label is defined just before the heading, which is fine, but consider adding a cross‑reference to this label from the "Capturing output" section of the tutorial index so readers can discover the note more easily.
The entry for pytest 8.4 should probably be "8.4+" to indicate that the minimum version applies to 8.4 and later, matching the style of the other rows.
Hard‑coding the version string ('9.0.2') makes the docs stale when the package is released again. Use the existing |version| substitution (or similar) instead of a literal version number.

rows.title: [truncate explanation] Fix edge case when we truncate due to max_chars

outcomes.text: If `_truncate_by_char_count` returns an empty list (possible when `max_chars` is very small), `truncated_explanation[-1] += "..."` will raise an IndexError. Guard against an empty `truncated_explanation` before appending the ellipsis.

The current computation of `truncated_line_count` adds `int(need_to_truncate_char)`. This counts a hidden line even when the character‑based truncation removed only part of a line, which can make the "X line(s) hidden" message off by one. Consider mirroring the original logic that distinguishes full‑line removal from partial truncation.

Appending "..." unconditionally may produce duplicate ellipsis strings (e.g., "......") because `_truncate_by_char_count` already returns a line consisting of "..." when it fully truncates a line. Detect this case and avoid adding a second ellipsis.

rows.title: fix(testing): `pytest.approx` correctly take account Mapping keys order to compare them

outcomes.text: Changing the key comparison from `set(self.expected.keys()) != set(other_side.keys())` to `self.expected.keys() != other_side.keys()` makes the check order‑sensitive. Mapping equality should ignore order, so this reverts the original bug fix and will cause false failures when the same keys appear in a different order. Revert to the set‑based comparison.

The loop now looks up `other_value = other_side[approx_key]` which is correct, but the previous `zip(..., strict=True)` also guarded against missing keys. Ensure that a clear error is raised if a key is missing rather than a `KeyError` bubbling up, matching the behavior of the original implementation.

The type annotation `dict[str, bytes]` requires Python 3.9+. pytest still supports Python 3.8, so this will raise a SyntaxError on older interpreters. Use `Dict[str, bytes]` from `typing` for broader compatibility.
`errno` is referenced in the exception handling block but the module is never imported, leading to a NameError at runtime. Add `import errno` at the top of the file.

Adding a fixed `junit.xml` filename for each matrix job can cause race conditions when jobs run in parallel – they will overwrite each other's report. Consider using a unique name per job (e.g. `junit-${{ matrix.tox_env }}.xml`) and adjust the Codecov upload step accordingly.

The `doctesting` environment now receives the `--junitxml` argument via `_PYTEST_TOX_POSARGS_JUNIT`. Doctests don't need a JUnit report, so this adds unnecessary file generation. You might want to limit the env var to the regular test envs only.

Changelog entries should follow the project's format: include a short title line, a reference to the issue number, and a blank line before the body. Adjust the file to match other `*.contrib.rst` entries.
